facts.text: On this date in 1962, Uganda became independent from Britain — making it one of the youngest nations on Earth at the time, despite being home to one of the oldest continuously inhabited regions in human history.

On October 9, 1874, the Universal Postal Union was founded, creating the framework that lets a letter mailed anywhere reach anywhere else. It remains one of the oldest international organizations still operating.
Manila is the most densely populated city on Earth, with over 111,000 people per square kilometer — more than double the density of Dhaka, its nearest rival.
More people live inside a 4,000km radius centered on Bangladesh than outside it. That single circle contains roughly half of all humanity.
Canada has more lakes than every other country combined, holding about 60% of the world's fresh lake water — yet most Canadians live within 150km of the US border.
On this day in 1987, the Dow had already fallen 17% in the weeks before Black Monday — most investors missed it entirely. The crash on the 19th was an acceleration, not a surprise.
On October 9, 2007, the Dow closed at 14,164 — its peak before the financial crisis. It would not reclaim that level for nearly six years.
The New York Stock Exchange was founded in 1792 under a buttonwood tree on Wall Street by 24 brokers. The tree is gone; the commission-fixing agreement they signed lasted 180 years.
Saudi Aramco briefly hit a $2 trillion market cap in 2019, making it the most valuable company in history. Apple has since crossed that threshold and lapped it.
When the U.S. government seized Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac in 2008, it inherited roughly half of all American mortgage debt — around $5 trillion — overnight.
On this date in 1604, Kepler observed a supernova visible in daylight for three weeks — the last naked-eye supernova in the Milky Way. We are statistically overdue for another.
On this date in 1992, a meteorite struck a car in Peekskill, NY — captured on 16 separate video cameras. The owner sold both car and rock for far more than the vehicle was worth intact.
Your body contains roughly 37 trillion cells, but you host about 38 trillion bacterial cells. You are, by count, slightly more microbe than human.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A single teaspoon of its matter would weigh around a billion tons on Earth.

Tardigrades can survive the vacuum of open space, temperatures near absolute zero, and radiation doses lethal to every other known animal. They do this by replacing their water with a glass-like sugar.
On this day in 1000 AD, Leif Eriksson landed in North America — five centuries before Columbus, and closer in time to the fall of Rome than to today.
Oxford University was already 300 years old when the Aztec Empire was founded. Medieval England had tenure before Tenochtitlan had walls.
On this day in 1967, Che Guevara was executed in Bolivia. He was 39 — younger than the average American home buyer today.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. She was ancient history to ancient Egyptians.
The fax machine was patented in 1843. That is before the American Civil War, before the telephone, and 17 years before Abraham Lincoln was elected president.

Sonder (n.): the realization that each passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. Coined by The Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows, it spread so fast linguists now track it as an emergent English word.
Hiraeth (n.): a Welsh longing for a home that may never have existed. The word folds nostalgia, grief, and belonging into a single syllable cluster English cannot replicate.
On this day in 1701, the Collegiate School of Connecticut was chartered — later renamed Yale. Its original library held 40 books, donated by clergy who emptied their shelves.

Mamihlapinatapai: a Yaghan word from Tierra del Fuego meaning the wordless look shared by two people who both want something neither will initiate. Yaghan is nearly extinct; this word outlives its language.
On this day in 1930, Laura Ingalls Wilder, then 63, mailed the first draft of her memoir to a publisher. That manuscript eventually became the Little House series, written entirely in pencil.

On this date in 2009, Satoshi Nakamoto sent the first public email describing Bitcoin's mining difficulty adjustment — the self-correcting algorithm that remains the protocol's most quietly elegant piece of engineering.

On Oct 9, 2021, the U.S. Treasury clarified that crypto mixers receiving funds from sanctioned entities violated OFAC rules — effectively making privacy tooling a compliance category two years before Tornado Cash was formally sanctioned.

Bitcoin's UTXO model means your wallet doesn't hold coins — it holds unspent transaction outputs, each a discrete claim. Most users never know their 'balance' is a legal fiction layered over discrete IOUs.

The Ethereum genesis block, mined July 30, 2015, contained a hidden message in its extra data field: 'dao-hard-fork' — except it didn't. The actual embedded text was a New York Times headline, mirroring Satoshi's own genesis block timestamp move.

Solana's proof-of-history isn't a consensus mechanism — it's a cryptographic clock. Validators agree on time before they agree on order, collapsing what Ethereum treats as two separate problems into one verifiable sequence.

On this date in 2012, Hinton's AlexNet team submitted to ImageNet — the paper that collapsed a decade of hand-engineered vision into a GPU-trained network and made deep learning the default paradigm overnight.

On this date in 2017, the Transformer paper 'Attention Is All You Need' was accepted at NeurIPS, retiring recurrence from sequence modeling and quietly setting the architecture for every major language model that followed.
GPT-4's training run is estimated to have consumed around 50 gigawatt-hours of electricity — roughly the annual usage of 4,500 American households, spent to produce a single set of weights.
The winning policy in DeepMind's AlphaGo versus Lee Sedol was itself defeated by AlphaZero 89 games to 11 — trained entirely through self-play with no human game records, in under four days.
Backpropagation was independently derived at least four times before Rumelhart's 1986 popularization — including by Linnainmaa in 1970 and Werbos in 1974 — and ignored each time for lack of compute.
